title: Clamber: Climbing Sound Effects
shortText: 660 climbing SFX: grab, climb, shimmy, slip, let go on 12 holds, 3 weights, 3 takes, 12 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
Every hold a game climbs, one hand on all of them

648 climbing sounds on 12 holds: grab, let go, shimmy, climb up, climb down and slip, at three body weights, 3 takes in every cell, plus 12 seamless climbing loops.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 38 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. A grab and a climb up on every one of the 12 holds, all six actions on the wooden ladder and the rope, a climb up a rock face at light, medium and heavy, the three takes of a chain grab, and two climbing loops.

A grid, not a handful of one shots

The climbing packs we read give you a few dozen one shots for one kind of wall. A climbing system asks for a sound by STATE: which hold, what the hands are doing, how heavy the climber is. So every hold here (rope, cargo net, vine, tree bark, wooden ladder, rock face, brick ledge, pipe, metal ladder, chain, chain link fence and ice wall) exists for every action (grab, let go, shimmy, climb up, climb down, slip) at every weight (light, medium, heavy), with 3 takes in every cell.

Wiring it is one string: "climb_" + hold + "_" + action + "_" + weight + "_" + take. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: inside each weight, every hold differs from every other hold for the same action, and every action from every other action on the same hold (1728 pairs, none alike), and on all 72 hold and action combinations the heavier climber is darker than the lighter one at both steps (the lightest at least 1.59x brighter than the heaviest).

One hand on every hold

Every sound is made by one hand model: the same palm and finger closure, the same boot, the same body mass and the same timing for each action. Only the hold changes: struck rungs, a pipe, brick, rock, a trunk and an ice wall; friction, creak and sway for the rope, the net and the vine; links and wire that keep moving after the hand lands. A character who climbs from a rope onto a brick ledge changes hold, not sound library.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by hold, action, weight and take.
  • 12 seamless climbing loops, one per hold, 4 seconds each, with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 216 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness, so a long climb does not machine gun one sample.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 2.99 dB.
  • The weight names are the same three our footstep pack uses, so one character weight setting drives both the feet and the hands.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, FMOD and Wwise and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 5962 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our movement packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in Footfall, Wade and Harness and against the climbing cues already in our other packs (584760 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 584760 of 584760 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json. The packs share a grammar; they do not share files.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not recordings of real climbing: a game that wants recorded realism wants a recorded library. No voice in this pack (no grunts, no breaths) and nothing musical. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover illustration is AI generated, and the store graphics are made by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Footfall, the footstep matrix: twelve surfaces, four gaits, the same three weights.
  • Wade, wet and submerged movement for the same characters.
  • Harness, the cloth, armour and gear a climber is wearing.
  • Threshold, metroidvania ability gates and unlocks.
  • Longhaul, survival, gathering and the camp at night.
